gaps.sentence: There were ___ people in the lift, and it broke down.
gaps.explanation: 'Too many' is used before countable plurals like people; 'too much' is for uncountables.

gaps.sentence: Three out of four respondents — that is, the ___ — supported the change.
gaps.hint: three out of four = more than half
gaps.explanation: Three out of four is more than half, so 'the majority' is the correct label.

gaps.sentence: The village is remote and has ___ facilities — not even a post office.
gaps.hint: negative meaning with a countable plural
gaps.explanation: 'Few facilities' means almost none, which matches 'not even a post office'; 'facilities' is countable.

gaps.sentence: There were ___ interruptions this year, so the ceremony ran far more smoothly.
___ of the workforce is part-time now.
gaps.hint: pattern: ___ of + specific group; singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Half of the workforce is ...' is the correct pattern; 'the half of' is not used in this position.

gaps.sentence: There are two cafes here, but ___ of them is open on Mondays.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of them is open' is correct for two items with a singular verb; 'both' and 'all' would need 'are'.

gaps.sentence: I haven't got ___ cash on me — I'll pay by card.
gaps.explanation: 'Any' is the normal quantifier in negative sentences; 'haven't got no cash' would be a double negative.

gaps.sentence: ___ candidate was given five minutes to speak.
gaps.hint: one at a time, singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Each candidate was given' — singular agreement; 'all candidate' is wrong.
